newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open weaker in quiet activity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open weaker in quiet activity.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened slightly weaker in quiet trade on Tuesday on the back of strength in the Canadian dollar and some weakness in the bond market, dealers said.

"We came in and saw some selling in the morning, but then it dried up with the currency getting stronger," said one T-bill dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "A lot of people are currency watchers today and we expect to see some buyers emerge with the strength in the (Canada) dollar."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.12 percent from 3.11 percent at Monday's close.
Analysts said the fact that the Canadian dollar has held onto recent gains had helped to offset a bearish tone in the money market.

The Canadian dollar opened slightly weaker on Tuesday at C$1.3792 (US$0.7251) after the unit came under pressure from overnight selling against the Japanese yen, but the unit rebounded to C$1.3757 (US$0.7267) in mid-morning trade.
"There is still a bearish bias in the market with the (weekly T-bill) auction today and the supply coming out," the trader said. "We see it coming off another five beeps from where it is right now."
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.41 percent from 3.38 percent on Monday. The one-year T-bill dipped to yield 3.91 percent from 3.89 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.20 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
